chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Bechet, Johnny Dodds and the unknown high-B-flat trumpeter
summary: At the Elite No. 1 in Chicago he heard Johnny Dodds and an unidentified trumpeter who hit a high B-flat; Bechet could not say who the visitors were.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, how was Bechet playing at that time?
Bechet, I think was simply terrific, 'cause I heard Johnny Dodds. Johnny Dodds was at the Elite No. 1, in Chicago.
heard another trumpet player that made a high B-flat, I just told you about, and on the same evening.--
Did you know who the other trumpet player was?

No, I couldn't get close enough. And Mr. & Mrs. Mullins, they said, "Oh, let's get out of here, it's so smokey," and everything else. But I always tried to find out who he was. He was a good trumpet player.
There was a New Orleans trumpet player around at that time called Sugar Johnny Smith, and there was George Mitchell.
I think he might have been.
Oh, yes. He might have been one of them. I don't know. I tried to find out who he was, but -- I even tried to find out through Bechet, but Bechet didn't even go know.
didn't seem to know. He said, "They're so many of them out there, they come and they play just to have a good time, and they never tell us who they are."
